lead: Voters rejected data centers in 38 of 40-plus ballot races and Abbott lost Texas by 700,000, while data-center stocks fell. Cat Wu leaves Anthropic for OpenAI, Anthropic signs its first content deal with the AP, and OpenAI says it patched 948 Linux privilege-escalation bugs for $1.2M.

sections.title: The ballot box vs. the data center
sections.intro: Voters reject data centers in 38 of 40+ ballot races, Abbott loses Texas by 700,000, and data-center stocks fall even as the market rallies.

sections.title: The supply chain squeeze
sections.intro: AI demand now crowds out PCBs on top of RAM and GPUs, and Arm's royalty miss hints at a mixed chip picture.

sections.title: The money keeps moving
sections.intro: SpaceX's chip debt gets syndicated and Isomorphic Labs eyes $5B at $50B.

sections.title: The agent economy
sections.intro: Garry Tan's $200K token bill, a venting piece on agent tools, and a CLI that tests whether agents can use your docs.

sections.title: The talent and the lobby
sections.intro: Cat Wu moves from Anthropic to OpenAI, and Anthropic signs its first content deal, with the AP.

sections.title: The security desk
sections.intro: OpenAI says it validated and patched 948 Linux privilege-escalation bugs for $1.2M.

sections.title: The consumer push
sections.intro: Images 2.6 brings GIFs to ChatGPT; 4 billion images a week.

sections.title: The scam economy
sections.intro: Platforms take any ad that pays, and the spam now fakes close reading.

sections.title: The open web at stake
sections.intro: Doctorow on why banning scraping and weakening CDA 230 would entrench the giants.

sections.title: The job market and the roadmap
sections.intro: UK entry-level postings now ask for AI, Meta retires fruit codenames, and China blocks SoftBank's robotics deal.

sections.title: The open-weight race
sections.intro: New open and near-open models arrive from Tencent, Cognition and Ricursive, and Delangue argues risk lives in closed labs.

sections.title: The research shelf
sections.intro: Lean formalization of the Stacks Project, AlphaEvolve's code, and a paper arguing long context is overrated.

sections.title: The business desk
sections.intro: An Intuit CEO interview and Perplexity's Decisions API.
